text:
maya_support: FYI customer (tenant: brightco) hitting spikes of 5xx + timeouts for hosted inference since ~08:10 UTC. They reported slow tail latencies and a stream of 502/504s.

jason_oncall: seeing similar alerts in the gateway. p95 tail jumped to ~18s, p99 to 45s. Lots of request_queue_rejects in logs.

rachel_infra: grabbing logs/metrics now. initial glance: continuous-batcher backlog growth and queue_depth saturating.

sam_runtime: any recent deploys to batching or kv-cache?

maya_support: customer says nothing changed on their side; they provided a few request IDs. attaching their curl repro: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-4k","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":512}'
```

olivia_sre: I'm seeing gateway logs with repeated: 
```
ERROR gateway: enqueue failed: request_queue_full tenant=brightco queue_depth=512 max_depth=512
WARN batcher: continuous-batcher backlog=128 active_batchers=4 kv_cache_ready=false
ERROR runtime: serve_timeout: tail_timeout=true request_id=rdw-3f2b
```

sam_runtime: kv_cache_ready=false is alarming — could mean KV cache bootstrap slow. continuous-batcher backlog=128 suggests batching is not draining. Might be a hotspot causing some batchers to block.

jason_oncall: Correlating with infra: one node in pool reported GPU OOM and restarted around 08:05 UTC, then autoscaler replaced it. Could have caused temporary reduced throughput and caused queue to pile.

nikhil_cs: customer ramp was normal, but they started a new batch run at 08:07 (500 concurrent requests over 2m).

maya_support: customer wants ETA and whether we can waive charges for errors.

olivia_sre: immediate mitigations: 1) temporary tenant-level rate-limit (slowdown) 2) bump queue_depth soft limit for the pool to 768 3) force flush KV cache on lagging nodes 4) reduce batch size threshold for continuous-batcher to favor latency over throughput.

sam_runtime: I can push a hotfix to reduce batcher.min_batch_size from 16 -> 8 and lower max_batch_delay from 40ms -> 20ms in pool config. That should reduce tail but increase tokens/cost.

rachel_infra: I can bump queue depth on the pool but need to coordinate with ops for node memory checks. Suggest doing it for 10m window.

jason_oncall: +1 to short-term rate-limit + config change. I'll also enable additional debugging for batcher goroutines and kv cache.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated: runtime-config/continuous-batcher@hotfix-2890012345 -> canary (3/10).

olivia_sre: Applied tenant throttle (brightco) 60rps. Observing immediate drop in 5xxs. p95 drops to ~6s.

sam_runtime: hotfix rolled to canary. Monitoring.

maya_support: customer notified of throttling and mitigation. They've accepted temporary throttling and asked for root cause follow-up.

olivia_sre: After hotfix, backlog reduced from 128 -> 12 in 2m. queue_depth saw headroom. KV cache bootstrap logs show one node lagging (disk IO high) but others healthy.

jason_oncall: Next steps for RCA: 1) investigate OOM/restart that preceded saturation 2) look at autoscaler timing and replacement delay 3) review continuous-batcher heuristics for bursty tenants 4) add more observability on per-tenant queue occupancy and per-batcher latency.

nikhil_cs: I'll coordinate a postmortem and credits request with the customer. Please include timeline and corrective actions.

maya_support: thanks. filing incident with notes -> https://redwood/internal/incidents/INC-2890012345 (add logs & timeline).

olivia_sre: Adding follow-up action: implement per-tenant early-throttle when queue_depth > 70% for 30s to avoid full saturation.

sam_runtime: also adding an integration test that simulates node replacement with steady client bursts to validate batching recovery.

jason_oncall: closing loop for now — system stable, 5xxs dropped to baseline, customer in support thread. Will update postmortem draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
